title: Do people trust China, the U.S. or the EU to regulate AI?
summary: Trust in China, the U.S. and the EU to regulate AI is tied to overall favorability. Many people trust their own country more than any other regulator.

title: Appendix: Detailed tables
Concerns about AI are especially widespread in high-income countries
summary: People in high-income countries are more likely than those in less wealthy nations to be concerned about AI, as well as its impact on jobs and economic inequality.

title: Who has heard or read a lot about AI, and how is awareness changing?
summary: Majorities in most of 37 countries surveyed have at least some awareness of AI. In some places, the share who has heard a lot about it has increased since last year.

title: What do young people around the world think about AI?
summary: A 37-country survey finds that young adults are particularly worried about AI leading to fewer jobs. Still, they're more likely than older people to feel both excited and concerned about AI.

title: Globally, More People Expect AI to Cause Job Loss Than Growth
summary: Amid a mix of concern and excitement about AI, a 37-country survey finds pessimism about its potential impact on jobs and economic inequality.
